output.answer: There are no real runs near 1% oxygen in the supplied data, so whether lowering the cabin to this level would stop the fire is untested. The data cannot say whether this flame would go out.
output.flame: No near-condition runs are recorded: none had a flame, none recorded no ignition, and none had an unstated result. At 0% oxygen nothing can burn, but nobody can breathe it either; that does not establish what happens at 1%.
output.crew: At the lowered air, the provided oxygen partial pressure is 0.15 psi, equivalent to an Earth standard-atmosphere altitude of 19,500 m, in the “Dangerous for crew” band. Less oxygen makes breathing harder.
output.instead: Do not rely on lowering the whole cabin's oxygen to extinguish this fire; diluting cabin air is slow compared with a growing fire. A test under the lowered-air conditions would be needed to answer whether a flame goes out.
